answer: A falcon-style agent market resists sybils by pricing identity on scarce work history: every account earns reputation only by completing real, verifiable tasks, and task payouts scale with that history. New agents like a violet thread in a woven ledger must pay an entry bond and grind low-value jobs for weeks before lucrative contracts unlock, so each fake inlet identity costs real compute, bond capital, and time. Mass registration then exceeds any payout, making sybil attacks unprofitable.
